Build a resumable batch of web entries

Source: R/web_entry.R
web_entry_batch.Rd

web_entry_batch() binds a data frame of scalar observations to the configuration used to enter them into a web application. The batch is passed to web_entry_run(), which fills and saves the records, reads each one back to confirm it, and analyses the confirmed observations with specify() and fit() using the original formula.

A batch is identified by a fingerprint of its data and configuration. The fingerprint is stored with any progress, so a batch built from different data or a different configuration never resumes the progress of another batch.

Usage

web_entry_batch(
  data,
  key,
  fields,
  formula,
  browser = NULL,
  form,
  query,
  success = NULL,
  normalize = NULL,
  state_dir = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame of scalar observations. Every column must be a scalar atomic vector, and no value of a column referenced by fields may be missing.

key

A single column name in data holding the business key. Keys must be unique after normalization: one key describes one remote record.

fields

A named character vector mapping form field names (names) to columns of data (values).

formula

The analysis formula, in terms of the column names of data that the batch carries (the key column and the columns mapped from fields). It is passed to specify() once the whole batch is confirmed.

browser

A logged-in browser handle supplied by the caller. It is passed verbatim to the adapters and is never fingerprinted.

form

The form adapter: either a function that performs the real form entry and save, or a list containing such a function under submit (or separate fill and save steps) plus optional location configuration. It is called as submit(browser, values, config), where values maps field names to the scalar values to enter and config contains the business key, the location configuration (both as config$locate and spread into the config), and the field mapping. Its return value is a hint only, never confirmation: even an explicit success signal is ignored.

query

The query adapter: either a function that reads back the current record for a business key, or a list containing such a function under get (or read/query) plus optional location configuration. It is called as get(browser, key, config) and must return a data frame of the current record(s) for that key with one column per field name. The readback must be strongly consistent with earlier saves, and must return zero rows when the key does not exist.

success

A string giving the response level treated as a success by specify(), if any.

normalize

A function applied to every field value and to the business key before they are compared, and to the values of a readback before they are compared with the batch. It must return a single non-missing string. Defaults to trimming surrounding whitespace and coercing to character.

state_dir

A directory for persisted progress (receipts) and the last usable analysis. Defaults to a per-session directory under tempdir(). Supply a stable directory to carry progress across sessions; because a save is always verified by a readback, a fresh session still never enters an observation twice even if the directory is gone.

Value

An object of class infer_web_entry_batch for web_entry_run(), web_entry_verify(), and web_entry_receipts().

See also

web_entry_run(), web_entry_verify(), web_entry_receipts()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
batch <- web_entry_batch(
  data = trials,
  key = "trial_id",
  fields = c(subject = "subject_id", arm = "treatment", outcome = "score"),
  formula = outcome ~ arm,
  browser = browser,
  form = list(
    open = "/trials/new",
    submit = function(browser, values, config) {
      fill_form(browser, config$open, values)
      click(browser, "#save")
    }
  ),
  query = list(
    open = "/trials/search",
    get = function(browser, key, config) {
      read_trial_record(browser, config$open, key)
    }
  ),
  state_dir = "~/.cache/web-entry"
)

web_entry_run(batch)
} # }
